import math
from math import fsum


def _symmetric_eigendecomposition(matrix):
    """Return eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix.

    The cyclic Jacobi method is used.  ``eigenvectors`` is returned as a list
    of columns, i.e. ``eigenvectors[row][column]``.
    """
    n = len(matrix)
    if n == 0:
        return [], []

    a = [[float(value) for value in row] for row in matrix]
    vectors = [[1.0 if i == j else 0.0 for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]

    scale = max(
        (abs(a[i][j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n)),
        default=0.0,
    )
    if scale == 0.0:
        return [0.0] * n, vectors

    # Cyclic Jacobi rotations annihilate off-diagonal entries.  A handful of
    # sweeps is normally enough; the cap guards against pathological input.
    for _ in range(100):
        largest_off_diagonal = 0.0
        for p in range(n - 1):
            for q in range(p + 1, n):
                apq = a[p][q]
                largest_off_diagonal = max(largest_off_diagonal, abs(apq))
                if abs(apq) <= 1e-16 * scale:
                    continue

                app = a[p][p]
                aqq = a[q][q]
                tau = (aqq - app) / (2.0 * apq)
                if tau >= 0.0:
                    t = 1.0 / (tau + math.sqrt(1.0 + tau * tau))
                else:
                    t = -1.0 / (-tau + math.sqrt(1.0 + tau * tau))
                c = 1.0 / math.sqrt(1.0 + t * t)
                s = t * c

                for k in range(n):
                    if k != p and k != q:
                        akp = a[k][p]
                        akq = a[k][q]
                        a[k][p] = c * akp - s * akq
                        a[k][q] = s * akp + c * akq
                        a[p][k] = a[k][p]
                        a[q][k] = a[k][q]

                a[p][p] = c * c * app - 2.0 * s * c * apq + s * s * aqq
                a[q][q] = s * s * app + 2.0 * s * c * apq + c * c * aqq
                a[p][q] = 0.0
                a[q][p] = 0.0

                for k in range(n):
                    vkp = vectors[k][p]
                    vkq = vectors[k][q]
                    vectors[k][p] = c * vkp - s * vkq
                    vectors[k][q] = s * vkp + c * vkq

        if largest_off_diagonal <= 1e-15 * scale:
            break

    return [a[i][i] for i in range(n)], vectors


def _solve_least_squares(gram, rhs):
    """Solve ``gram @ x = rhs`` for a symmetric positive-semidefinite gram.

    A pseudoinverse is formed from the eigendecomposition.  This yields the
    minimum-norm solution when the system is rank deficient, instead of
    failing or arbitrarily choosing a free variable.
    """
    n = len(rhs)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    eigenvalues, eigenvectors = _symmetric_eigendecomposition(gram)
    largest_eigenvalue = max((abs(value) for value in eigenvalues), default=0.0)
    if largest_eigenvalue == 0.0:
        return [0.0] * n

    tolerance = largest_eigenvalue * max(n, 1) * 1e-12
    projected_rhs = [
        fsum(eigenvectors[i][k] * rhs[i] for i in range(n))
        for k in range(n)
    ]

    solution = [0.0] * n
    for k, eigenvalue in enumerate(eigenvalues):
        if eigenvalue > tolerance:
            factor = projected_rhs[k] / eigenvalue
            for i in range(n):
                solution[i] += eigenvectors[i][k] * factor
    return solution

        ):

    ordered_days = sorted(days)

    return [
        [
            temperatures.get((year, month, day))
            for day in ordered_days
        ]
        for year, month in ordered_months

import math


def feature_correlation_matrix(samples):
    """Return the pairwise Pearson correlation matrix for feature columns.

    ``samples`` is a sequence of equally-sized numeric rows.  Entry ``[i][j]``
    of the returned matrix is the Pearson correlation between columns ``i``
    and ``j``.

    A constant feature has zero variance, so its Pearson correlation with any
    other feature is mathematically undefined.  Such correlations are
    represented as ``0.0`` here; the diagonal entries are always ``1.0``.
    """
    if not samples:
        return []

    num_rows = len(samples)
    num_features = len(samples[0])

    if num_features == 0:
        return []

    # Work by column.  Assuming the documented rectangular input shape, this
    # avoids repeatedly indexing into every row for every feature pair.
    columns = [list(column) for column in zip(*samples)]
    means = [sum(column) / num_rows for column in columns]
    centered = [
        [value - mean for value in column]
        for column, mean in zip(columns, means)
    ]
    sum_squares = [sum(value * value for value in column) for column in centered]

    matrix = [[0.0] * num_features for _ in range(num_features)]

    for i in range(num_features):
        matrix[i][i] = 1.0
        for j in range(i):
            denominator = math.sqrt(sum_squares[i] * sum_squares[j])
            if denominator == 0.0:
                correlation = 0.0
            else:
                covariance = sum(
                    left * right
                    for left, right in zip(centered[i], centered[j])
                )
                correlation = covariance / denominator
                # Guard against tiny floating-point overshoots outside [-1, 1].
                correlation = max(-1.0, min(1.0, correlation))

            matrix[i][j] = correlation
            matrix[j][i] = correlation

    return matrix

"""Utilities for extracting hyperlink targets from HTML pages."""

from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit


class _LinkExtractor(HTMLParser):
    """Collect the ``href`` attribute of every anchor start tag."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.hrefs = []

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower() != "a":
            return

        # HTML parsers use the first occurrence of a duplicate attribute.
        for name, value in attrs:
            if name.lower() == "href":
                self.hrefs.append(value if value is not None else "")
                break


def extract_page_links(html, base_url):
    """Return the resolved ``href`` of every ``<a>`` element in *html*.

    Links are returned in document order, duplicates included.  Relative
    references are resolved against *base_url*; absolute references are
    returned unchanged.
    """
    parser = _LinkExtractor()
    parser.feed(html)
    parser.close()

    links = []
    for href in parser.hrefs:
        # Preserve absolute URLs exactly as written.  References such as
        # "//host/path" have no scheme and are therefore resolved against
        # the page URL.
        if urlsplit(href).scheme:
            links.append(href)
        else:
            links.append(urljoin(base_url, href))
    return links

from collections import Counter
from statistics import mean, median


def augment_and_summarize(data_dict):
    """Add ``'a': 1`` to *data_dict* and summarize the resulting values.

    Returns the updated dictionary, a dictionary containing the mean, median,
    and mode (the smallest value in case of a tie), and a 10-bin histogram of
    the min-max scaled values.
    """
    data_dict['a'] = 1
    values = list(data_dict.values())

    counts = Counter(values)
    max_frequency = max(counts.values())
    mode = min(value for value, frequency in counts.items()
               if frequency == max_frequency)

    summary = {
        'mean': mean(values),
        'median': median(values),
        'mode': mode,
    }

    minimum = min(values)
    maximum = max(values)

    histogram = [0] * 10
    for value in values:
        if maximum == minimum:
            scaled = 0.0
        else:
            scaled = (value - minimum) / (maximum - minimum)

        # The last bin is closed, so a scaled value of exactly 1 belongs in bin 9.
        bin_index = min(9, int(scaled * 10))
        histogram[bin_index] += 1

    return data_dict, summary, histogram

    Each row is represented as a list of mutable text-part lists so that
    nested markup inside a cell can be handled by simply collecting the
    parser's data callbacks.  Cell strings are joined and stripped once
    parsing is complete.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.rows: list[list[list[str]]] = []
        self._open_rows: list[list[list[str]]] = []
        self._open_cells: list[tuple[list[list[str]], list[str]]] = []
        self._header_depth = 0

    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]) -> None:
        tag = tag.lower()

        if tag == "tr":
            row: list[list[str]] = []
            self.rows.append(row)
            self._open_rows.append(row)
            # A new row implicitly ends any still-open header context.
            self._header_depth = 0
        elif tag == "td":
            if self._open_rows:
                parts: list[str] = []
                row = self._open_rows[-1]
                row.append(parts)
                self._open_cells.append((row, parts))
            # A td starts cell data, so any previous header is no longer
            # the current cell context.
            self._header_depth = 0
        elif tag == "th":
            self._header_depth += 1

    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
        tag = tag.lower()

        if tag == "tr":
            if self._open_rows:
                row = self._open_rows.pop()
                # Discard cell contexts belonging to a row that has ended,
                # which also makes malformed (unclosed) rows harmless.
                self._open_cells = [
                    (cell_row, parts)
                    for cell_row, parts in self._open_cells
                    if cell_row is not row
                ]
            self._header_depth = 0
        elif tag == "td":
            if self._open_cells:
                self._open_cells.pop()
        elif tag == "th":
            if self._header_depth:
                self._header_depth -= 1

    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
        if self._header_depth == 0 and self._open_cells:
            self._open_cells[-1][1].append(data)

    tags is included, HTML entities are decoded, and surrounding
    whitespace is stripped from each cell.

"""Utilities for extracting a page title from HTML."""

import json
import re
from html import unescape
from html.parser import HTMLParser


_TITLE_END_RE = re.compile(r"</title(?=[\s/>])", re.IGNORECASE)

# Elements whose contents are raw text in HTML.  A <title> appearing inside
# one of these is text, not an actual title element.  Python's HTMLParser only
# has special handling for script/style, so the others are tracked here.
_RAW_TEXT_ELEMENTS = {
    "iframe",
    "noembed",
    "noframes",
    "noscript",
    "plaintext",
    "textarea",
    "xmp",
}


class _TitleLocator(HTMLParser):
    """Locate the first title element and capture its raw RCDATA body."""

    def __init__(self, source):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=False)
        self.source = source
        self._line_starts = [0]
        self._line_starts.extend(match.end() for match in re.finditer("\n", source))
        self._raw_text_element = None
        self.found = False
        self.title_raw = None

    def _source_offset(self):
        line, column = self.getpos()
        return self._line_starts[line - 1] + column

    def _capture_title(self, content_start):
        match = _TITLE_END_RE.search(self.source, content_start)
        content_end = match.start() if match else len(self.source)
        self.title_raw = self.source[content_start:content_end]
        self.found = True

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if self.found:
            return

        tag = tag.lower()
        if self._raw_text_element is not None:
            # Raw-text elements do not contain markup.  (HTMLParser itself
            # skips script/style bodies, but it tokenizes the other raw-text
            # elements, so suppress any apparent tags there.)
            return

        if tag in _RAW_TEXT_ELEMENTS:
            self._raw_text_element = tag
            return

        if tag == "title":
            start_tag = self.get_starttag_text() or ""
            content_start = self._source_offset() + len(start_tag)
            self._capture_title(content_start)

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):
        if self.found:
            return
        tag = tag.lower()
        if self._raw_text_element is None and tag == "title":
            # In practice title is not a void element.  Treat the explicit
            # self-closing form as an empty title rather than consuming the
            # remainder of the document.
            self.title_raw = ""
            self.found = True

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if self._raw_text_element is not None and tag.lower() == self._raw_text_element:
            self._raw_text_element = None


def extract_title_json(html):
    """Return the first HTML title as ``{"title": ...}`` encoded as JSON.

    ``None`` is used when the markup contains no title element.  Character
    references in the title's text are decoded.
    """

    locator = _TitleLocator(html)
    locator.feed(html)
    locator.close()

    if not locator.found:
        title = None
    else:
        title = unescape(locator.title_raw)

    return json.dumps({"title": title})
